hypothesis: KDP crystals grown at 35°C with faster cooling rate of 1.5°C/hour will still yield acceptable purity while reducing total growth time
context: Follow-up to run_001 baseline. Testing whether tripling the cooling rate (0.5 → 1.5°C/hour) compromises crystal quality enough to matter. If acceptable, faster cooling saves 4-5 hours per batch. Same reagent concentrations and starting conditions as run_001. Key risk is thermal shock during nucleation — faster cooling narrows the stable window and increases sensitivity to any temperature excursion.

stages.name: equilibration
stages.description: Hold at 35°C. Allow solution to reach thermal and chemical steady state. Impurity readings may be slightly elevated (up to 25 ppm) during this phase — this is normal.

stages.name: nucleation
stages.description: Faster cooling phase begins. Higher cooling rate makes this stage more sensitive than run_001. Treat warning_above as critical during this window. Any thermal excursion here is likely to produce polycrystalline growth.

stages.name: growth
stages.description: Crystals growing. Monitor impurity closely. Capture microscopy images every 30 minutes.

temperature_c.concern: At 1.5°C/hour cooling rate, the crystal lattice is more fragile than in run_001. Any temperature excursion during nucleation (hours 2-5) has a higher probability of causing cracking. Respond faster than baseline — do not wait for a second warning reading before acting.

impurity_ppm.concern: Rising impurity means crystals are dissolving. At faster cooling rates this can cascade quickly. If impurity rises alongside temperature, correct temperature first. Compare to run_001 at the same elapsed time to distinguish expected vs anomalous rise.

ph.concern: Same as run_001. pH above 7.5 causes irreversible KDP hydrolysis. Sudden jumps indicate contamination or probe malfunction.

temperature_high.note: Never reduce more than 1°C per cycle. At faster cooling rates, overcorrection risk is higher. Wait one full cycle before re-adjusting.

temperature_low.note: Warm slowly. Only intervene if below warning_below for two consecutive readings.

ph_high.note: Start with 5ml, wait 60s, re-read before adding more.

impurity_spike.note: Lower temp to encourage re-crystallization. Check temperature first — impurity spikes at faster cooling rates almost always follow a thermal excursion.

known_risks: Faster cooling rate increases nucleation sensitivity — any temperature spike during hours 2-5 is more likely to cause cracking than in run_001.
Temperature control lags 2-3 minutes after a setpoint change — wait a full cycle before re-adjusting.
Impurity may spike transiently at the start of cooling (hour 2) as the system adjusts to faster rate — observe for 2 readings before treating as an anomaly.
Cooling system may overshoot by 0.5-1°C on the first cycle — normal behavior.
key_findings: Temperature spike at hour 3 (40.1°C) caused by cooling system fault during nucleation — exceeded critical threshold
Agent intervened: reduced setpoint to 32°C; temperature recovered within 8 minutes but crystal damage already occurred
Final impurity 61.4 ppm above 30 ppm target — thermal shock dissolved partially-formed crystals
Crystal clarity 71% — below 90% target; polycrystalline growth observed in microscopy image
Faster cooling rate (1.5°C/hour) not recommended for KDP — nucleation window too narrow to tolerate excursions
